item.description:
The full-screen alert can no longer get stuck. Press Esc to dismiss it, or Return to join when there's a single meeting to join.
Connecting or disconnecting a display while an alert is up now works properly too — the alert redraws itself for the displays you actually have. Previously, unplugging a screen could leave the alert stranded with its buttons off-screen, and because it covers the menu bar there was no way to close it short of force-quitting.
The tray menu now also shows which version you're running, just above Check for Updates.

Double-booked or back-to-back meetings that start at the same time now show up as a single full-screen alert listing all of them, each with its own Join button, instead of one alert silently replacing another before you could see it.

First stable release. Heads Up puts a full-screen alert on every display right before your meetings start, so you actually see it — pulls from your calendars, finds the Zoom/Meet/Teams link automatically, and lets you snooze or join straight from the alert.
What's new since 0.5.3: - Launch at login, offered on first run and adjustable anytime in Settings - Update notifications now show real release notes instead of a bare changelog link
Recent fixes: - Snoozing an alert no longer reopens it within seconds — it now actually waits out the snooze duration you picked - Join links wrapped by Microsoft Defender Safe Links (common on Microsoft 365) now resolve to the real Zoom/Meet/Teams URL instead of falling back to the wrong link - Fixed Calendar access never prompting on notarized builds - Real copyright notice in the About panel
